gloss: to get angry; to lose one's temper

definitions.gloss: to get angry; to be infuriated; to lose one's temper
definitions.explanation: To become angry, said of a sudden flare-up rather than a slow build. Literally 'it comes to the head.' Colloquial and forceful, used mainly about oneself in casual speech.

examples.japanese: その{言|い}い{方|かた}には{頭|あたま}に{来|き}た。
examples.english: The way he said that made me angry.

examples.japanese: {約束|やくそく}を{破|やぶ}られて{本当|ほんとう}に{頭|あたま}に{来|き}た。
examples.english: I was really furious that they broke their promise.

examples.japanese: {頭|あたま}に{来|き}たときは、{一度|いちど}{深呼吸|しんこきゅう}するようにしている。
examples.english: When I get angry, I make a point of taking one deep breath.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{注意|ちゅうい}しても{同|おな}じミスをくり{返|かえ}すので、さすがに{頭|あたま}に{来|き}てしまった。
examples.english: He kept making the same mistake no matter how often I warned him, so I finally lost my temper.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {頭|あたま} (head) + に + {来|く}る (to come). The past {頭|あたま}に{来|き}た is by far the most common form.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {頭|あたま}に{来|き}た: I got angry
- 〜に{頭|あたま}に{来|く}る: to get angry at ~
- {頭|あたま}に{来|き}て{何|なに}も{言|い}えなかった: to be too angry to speak

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {腹|はら}が{立|た}つ: to get angry — the standard, less charged expression, usable in writing
- ムカつく: to be pissed off — slangier and younger-sounding
- {怒|おこ}る: to get angry, to scold — the plain verb; also covers telling someone off

USAGE:
Too casual for business or formal writing; use {腹|はら}が{立|た}つ there. Said of another person it can sound accusatory, so it usually describes the speaker's own reaction.
